summary: The note describes the Evergreen Mile, a neighborhood Fun Run/Walkathon scheduled for 8 a.m. on September 10, 2023, created to bring neighbors together, promote health, and boost local businesses. Organized by residents Jessica Fernandez and Michael Johnson with volunteers, it features a 5K route and a community festival at the park. The piece highlights economic benefits, physical and mental well-being, and stronger community bonds, with quotes from local figures.
one_line: The Evergreen Mile, a September 10, 2023 neighborhood Fun Run/Walkathon, aims to build community, improve health, and boost local businesses.
key_facts: The Evergreen Mile is a Fun Run/Walkathon scheduled for 8 a.m. on September 10, 2023.
Jessica Fernandez and Michael Johnson, two long-time residents, conceived the Evergreen Mile because they saw the local park as an underutilized asset for community ties.
The event features a 5K route passing local shops and a farmers' market, ending with a community festival at the park.
The festival includes live music, food trucks, and interactive local business booths.
Local businesses, from sporting goods stores to cafes, reported increased traffic and sales in the weeks before the Run.
Harold Gomez, a local café owner, said customers were talking about the Run and buying water bottles or healthy snacks.
Local vendors will own the booths and refreshment stands on event day, expected to surge the economic stimulus.
Trisha Lee, a fitness expert and local gym owner, said the Fun Run supports both mental and physical well-being.
Schools have incorporated mini-runs into physical education curriculum to prepare children for the event.
Residents have been joining impromptu running groups and seeking advice on eating and exercising habits.
Anita Singh, community leader and volunteer coordinator, said neighbors are now carpooling, sharing tips, and looking out for each other.
The event is intended to become a neighborhood tradition, open to residents of all ages and backgrounds.
